summary: Under R&TC §17052, the only refundable California credit this childless 28-year-old can get is CalEITC. YCTC needs a child under 6, FYTC needs former-foster-youth status (unlisted, so false), and the renter's credit is nonrefundable. Federal AGI of about $22,534 is higher than earned income, so the phase-out runs on AGI. The last published amounts before the freeze are FTB's 2025 figures: $302 maximum, a $32,900 income limit, and the slow §17052(o) tail. At this AGI they give about $95, and the engine's $95.15 matches. The 2026 CCPI indexing (3.4%) was only announced in FTB Tax News after 2026-07-03, so the reference rests on frozen law and the $0 consensus is wrong: the 403(b) distribution is not disqualifying investment income, and the childless tail runs out to about $32,900.
